title: Geometry-based Schrödinger Bridges for Trustworthy Multimodal Fusion
claim: Prediction confidence can be high on wrong inputs, but geometric transport energy exposes unreliable or conflicting data and corrects the decision.
layout: 2 grouped panels (a),(b), left-to-right; stacked rows of 2-D plots and bars
description: The figure has two large groups. Group (a), Intra-modal Analysis, is a 2×3 grid. The top row shows a latent-space scatter of two interleaved moon-shaped manifolds (purple and blue) with a red OOD cross, then a sigmoid confidence curve that peaks at the OOD point labeled 'High Confidence', then a bar chart giving 99% for Class A and 1% for Class B. The bottom row shows a vector flow field with a red arrow marking a long transport path, then a rising red energy curve labeled 'High Energy (Reject)', then a regulated 50/50 bar chart. Group (b), Inter-modal Analysis, shows two latent spaces with ambiguous points joined by a gold 'Bridge Transport' arrow. Beside them are three step bar charts: low confidence, high cost, and a final decision in which the gold geometric fusion bar (0.95) beats the baseline (0.57). Pastel purple and blue are used for the data, red for failure and gold for the proposed fix.
caption: Overview of the proposed Geometry-based Multimodal Fusion (GMF). (a) Intra-modal Analysis: We utilize Rectified Flow to estimate how much correction an input needs in latent space. Noisy inputs or outliers require higher transport energy (squared velocity magnitude), serving as a geometric indicator of unreliability. (b) Inter-modal Analysis: Semantic conflicts are detected by measuring the high cross-modal transport costs between mismatched modalities, ensuring that conflicting information does not corrupt the joint decision.
abstract: Real-world multimodal systems must be robust against low-quality data, such as sensor noise, incomplete multimodal data and conflicting inputs. However, existing trustworthy fusion methods rely on the model's own prediction confidence to judge data quality. This creates a circular dependency: when a model is confident but wrong, these methods fail to detect the error. To break this loop, we propose Geometry-based Multimodal Fusion (GMF). Instead of relying on predictions, we evaluate reliability by measuring how much transport correction the input needs in latent space. We implement Diffusion SchrÃ¶dinger Bridge transport with Rectified Flow, where the squared initial velocity gives an efficient learned correction score. Valid data has low squared velocity magnitude, while noisy, incomplete data or conflicting data requires stronger transport correction. This geometry-based reliability signal acts as an independent judge, effectively flagging unreliable inputs even when the classifier is fooled. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GMF significantly improves robustness against severe sensor noise and semantic conflicts compared to confidence-based baselines.
